weightingGuidance: Higher weight on: debt service, debt roll-forward, debt sizing, reserve accounts (DSRA), cash waterfall sequencing, cash sweep and lock-up mechanisms, covenant definitions and compliance, interest during construction, period flags, actuals cut-over, and distributions.

sourceModelSummary.model_purpose: A multi-entity operating and financial model for a fictional national railway system (Ruritania Railways) projecting freight, passenger and infrastructure operations, financing and consolidated financial statements over a 30-year horizon.
sourceModelSummary.industry: railway transport (freight, passenger and infrastructure operations)
sourceModelSummary.timeline: 30-year annual projection from January 2010 to January 2039 (Year 1 to Year 30)
key_drivers: Freight and passenger traffic volume growth (net ton-km / passenger-km)
Track access charges and tariffs (R$ per unit)
Debt structure and interest rates across multiple lenders and currencies

sheet_map.Cover: Empty/title sheet, likely containing model name and branding only.
sheet_map.Assumptions - General: Setup sheet where the user selects whether freight, passenger and infrastructure entities are integrated or separated, defining the model structure.
sheet_map.Assumptions - Freight: Entity-level input assumptions for the Ruritania Freight Rail Company including network length, staff, traffic volume and electric traction share.
sheet_map.Assumptions - Passenger: Entity-level input assumptions for the Ruritania Passenger Rail Company including network length, staff, traffic volume and electric traction share.
sheet_map.Assumptions - Infrastructure: Entity-level input assumptions for the Ruritania Railway Infrastructure Company including network length, staff, external freight traffic and electric traction share.
sheet_map.Assumptions - Consolidated: Additional headquarters/consolidation-level staffing assumptions shared across the three entities.
sheet_map.Calculations: Intermediate calculation sheet flagging which modeling periods are active for freight, passenger and infrastructure entities under different structure selections.
sheet_map.Balance sheet: Consolidated/entity balance sheet showing cash, receivables, inventory and other working capital items across the 30-year projection.
sheet_map.Income statement: Revenue and cost build-up by entity (freight, passenger revenue, track access charges, operating subsidy) feeding into consolidated profit.
sheet_map.Cash flow statement: Derivation of cash flow from net income, adding back interest, FX gains/losses and depreciation.
sheet_map.Charts - Consolidated: Chart data summarizing consolidated operating revenues and costs with CAGR calculations.
sheet_map.Charts - Freight: Chart data summarizing freight entity operating revenues and costs with CAGR.
sheet_map.Charts - Passenger: Chart data summarizing passenger entity operating revenues with CAGR.
sheet_map.Charts - Infrastructure: Chart data summarizing infrastructure entity operating revenues with CAGR.
sheet_map.Results - Consolidated: Summary output sheet showing average track-km, staff, traffic and growth statistics plus working capital days and initial debt for the consolidated group.
sheet_map.Results - Freight: Summary output sheet for freight entity including average staff, traffic, growth rate and financing/debt terms by lender.
sheet_map.Results - Passenger: Summary output sheet for passenger entity including average staff, traffic, growth rate and financing/debt terms by lender.
sheet_map.Results - Infrastructure: Summary output sheet for infrastructure entity including average staff, traffic, growth rate and financing/debt terms by lender.
sheet_map.Scenarios - Consolidated: Scenario analysis toggle and inputs allowing comparison of current vs base case values for key consolidated variables.
sheet_map.Scenarios - Freight: Scenario analysis toggle and inputs for freight-specific variables such as tariff, traffic growth and staff count.
sheet_map.Scenarios - Passenger: Scenario analysis toggle and inputs for passenger-specific variables such as fare, traffic growth and staff count.
sheet_map.Scenarios - Infra: Scenario analysis toggle and inputs for infrastructure-specific variables such as access charge rate and traffic growth.

immediate_observations: Cash and cash equivalents on the Balance sheet grow from 300 in 2010 to over 1 million by 2039 with no visible dividend or distribution outflow, suggesting a missing cash sweep or distribution mechanism.

Interest and finance expense declines toward near-zero by later years despite a rapidly growing balance sheet, which is inconsistent unless debt is being fully amortized - this should be checked against the debt schedules.

Growth rate figures for the same entity differ across sheets (e.g. freight growth appears as 0.32% in Scenarios - Freight but 1.95% in Assumptions - Freight and Results - Consolidated), indicating a possible inconsistency between assumption inputs and derived/scenario values.

The model uses a fictional country and entities (Ruritania), and column headers throughout (col3, col4, col19, etc.) are inconsistent or blank, suggesting this may be a generic template model rather than a live deal-specific model.

Debt financing spans multiple currencies (USD, EUR, R$) across Local, International, Multilateral and Regional banks, yet realized foreign exchange gains and losses are shown as zero in all periods, which seems inconsistent with multi-currency debt exposure.

The Assumptions - General sheet indicates the model can be run as integrated or separated entities, so care is needed to verify that Balance sheet, Income statement and Cash flow statement sheets correctly reflect the currently selected structure and are not double-counting or omitting entities.
sourceModelSummary.validation_focus: Verify consistency of growth rate and traffic assumptions between the Assumptions, Results and Scenario sheets for each entity; confirm the debt/interest schedule logic (multi-currency debt, interest declining to near-zero, and zero realized FX gains/losses despite foreign-currency loans); check for a missing dividend or cash distribution mechanism causing unrealistic cash accumulation on the Balance sheet; and confirm that the integrated vs separated entity structure selection correctly flows through to consolidated financial statements without double counting.
